newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
Robusta futures in London were mostly lower by the close. January lost $7 to close at $1,303 per tonne while March gave up $6 to close at $1,233 per tonne.

There were no fresh fundamental news to give the market direction but traders said the major factor in the coming months is the size of the 1997/98 Brazilian crop. So far preliminary estimates have varied widely from below 20 million 60-kg bags to as high as 32 million bags and compared with 26 to 28 million bags in 1996/97. Some Brazilian agronomists have put the coming crop at below 20 million bags although a more reliable assessment is not likely to emerge until the end of January. Most consumers remain skeptical and say that warnings of a smaller crop at this stage is nothing more than an attempt to boost prices and that it is much too early to give a precise estimate for 1997/98.

In New York arabica futures closed higher across the board although the market lost steam after talk of an increase in CSC certified stock figures. The market did not respond to reports from El Salvador that coffee shipments could be front loaded with an increased percentage being able to be fixed against the March contract. Traders said this could put pressure on the market if more coffee becomes available than anticipated. However, Ruben Pineda, the executive director of the Salvadoran Coffee Council told Reuters that the sale of coffee to March will be in accordance with the ACPC retention scheme.

The increase in US certified coffee stocks during the week ended December 6 of 2,000 bags is in line with expectations and should have limited impact on prices on Tuesday. December added 1.35 cents/lb to close at 113.10 cents/lb while March last traded 2.35 cents/lb higher at 105.60 cents/lb. The outer months added 2.20 to 1.15 cents/lb.

UNITED STATES - The CSC reported a 2,000 bag increase in US certified coffee stocks during the week ended December 6. While stocks in New York, New Orleans and San Francisco remained unchanged stocks in Miami rose by 2,000 bags to 2,019 bags. Moreover there were 11,750 bags pending grading in Miami.

UNITED STATES - For the week ended November 30 coffee roastings totalled approximately 400,000 60-kg bags, down from 415,000 bags the previous week and compared with 410,000 bags in the corresponding week one year ago, Complete Coffee Coverage said. Cumulative roastings totalled 16.065 million bags, versus 15.505 million bags in the same year-ago period.

UNITED KINGDOM - The UK imported 210,579 bags of coffee in August 1996, 11 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 1.988 million bags, 9.5 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 18 per cent to 2.783 million bags.

Main suppliers of green coffee in January/August 1996 were Costa Rica (167,100 vs 229,600 bags), Colombia (175,200 vs 119,500 bags), Indonesia (198,200 vs 153,500 bags) and Vietnam (185,400 vs 86,500 bags).

The country exported 369,500 bags of coffee in January/August 1996, slightly more than last year's figure of 367,300 bags. Total exports in calendar year 1995 fell by nearly 20 per cent to 538,400 bags.
